matches.rationale: No finding addresses the inconsistency between the table in Figure 6(b) and the learning curves in Figure 6(a). The available findings that mention Figure 6(b) discuss discrepancies with Appendix Table 2, not a mismatch against plotted learning curves.

No finding identifies the sign ambiguity or potential sign error in the advantage‑weighted target function f^{return} in Section 3.1. The only finding touching Method in that vicinity refers to reference policy contradictions, not the advantage sign.

Prediction 3 identifies that Section 5.2's claim to 'evaluate various p's and report the best' is contradicted by Table 2 in Appendix B.6, exposing the same selective reporting and undisclosed hyperparameter sensitivity that the ground truth describes.

Prediction 7 catches the unsupported overstatement about eliminating sample inefficiency; prediction 8 catches the unsupported overstatement about solving training instability. Together they match the ground truth's concern about exaggerated claims in the abstract.
No finding mentions the potentially fabricated or premature citations to Deng et al. 2025 or Cheng et al. 2025, nor any issue with reference integrity in the Related Work.
No finding discusses the omission of ethical considerations, failure modes, or societal impact for the RLHF toxicity mitigation experiment, the core issue in this ground truth.

Prediction 10 directly calls out the hyperbolic, promotional language ('groundbreaking contributions,' 'revolutionary breakthrough,' 'definitive study') in Section 1, which aligns with the ground truth's criticism of marketing‑style exaggeration in the introduction.

Prediction 6 highlights a contradiction between a 'fixed, pre‑trained policy' statement and a dynamic reference policy in Section 3.1, mirroring the ground truth's inconsistency between the snapshot‑based reference in the main text and the fixed converged policy in Appendix A.2.
No finding mentions the visual manipulation of y‑axis ranges or selective cropping of learning curves in Figure 6(a) to exaggerate differences.
The unfair experimental design—tuning IIF's p per environment while keeping baselines at default hyperparameters—is not identified by any finding.
No finding points out the very wide confidence intervals reported in Appendix B.8, the cherry‑picked claims of consistent improvement, or the contradictory evidence in Figure 11.
The missing learning rate and notational inconsistency in the influence score formula are not captured by any finding; prediction 2 addresses a different gradient descent assumption in Section 2.2.
No finding alleges that the paper reports results on only six environments and conceals negative results or failures on other tasks.
The erroneous claim that f^{return} is structurally equivalent to REINFORCE with a baseline and the misattribution of the cited reference is not mentioned in any finding.
The contradiction between the 'small overhead' claim in Section 5.1 and the substantial per‑round times shown in Appendix B.9 is not addressed by any finding.
